newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Ecuador Congress backs delaying telecoms sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador Congress backs delaying telecoms sell-off.

text.p: Ecuador's Congress has recommended putting off for 45 days plans to privatize part of telecommunications firm Emetel to introduce changes in legislation, the head of the Budget Commission said Monday.

Chairman Alvaro Perez told Reuters his commission backed the National Modernization Council's recommendations to change the privatization law "to allow for one international operator to manage both telephone companies, but with conditions."

The sale of 35 percent of Emetel had been due September 16. Five foreign companies bought the prospectus -- Italy's Stet SpA, Spain's Telefonica, GTE Corp and MCI Communications Inc of the United States and Korean Telecom.
Three of them -- Stet, Telefonica and GTE -- qualified.
But Perez said in an interview that deadline "definitely won't be met" and that the bidding process should go back to zero to take into account changes in the sale proceedure.

Emetel, which the government says is worth about $1.2 billion in total, was to be sold off in two operating arms, Andinatel and Pacifictel. But the government has now persuaded Congress to alter the telecoms sale legislation to allow one sole operator to control both companies.
"If the rules of the game changed for three operators, it's only fair that the others that did not participate because the companies were divided should have a chance now," he said.
Perez said Congress would debate the recommendations later Monday and there should be a second and final debate towards the end of the week.
((-- Maria Veronica Barreiros. Quito Newsroom +5932 258433 e-mail:reuters1@reutersecu.com.ec))
